input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges, the initial SUPPORTED verdict remains correct.

H1 (materiality challenge) is REFUTED: The fair value changes were material. E7 shows consolidated net income for fiscal 2026 was $22.3 billion, while E1 confirms that fair value changes on equity investments contributed a gain of $2.1 billion. This represents approximately 9.4% of total net income, which is clearly material and would meaningfully affect reported results.

H2 (adjusted metrics challenge) found NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE: The retrieved evidence (E10, E11, E12) only describes the accounting treatment and fair value changes but does not mention any adjusted or non-GAAP earnings metrics that exclude these fair value changes. The absence of such disclosure does not refute the claim.

H3 (classification challenge) is REFUTED: E13 and E15 explicitly confirm that fair value changes on equity investments are recognized in "other gains and losses" which are characterized as "non-operating items" (E15). This supports rather than contradicts the claim that they mask operating performance.

The evidence establishes: (1) fiscal 2026 net income was affected by a $2.1 billion gain from fair value changes on equity investments (E1, E3); (2) these are explicitly classified as non-operating items that fluctuate (E3, E15); and (3) the amount is material relative to total net income of $22.3 billion (E7). All material elements of the claim are supported.
